extracted.intended_audience: SEC reporting professionals, corporate counsel, accountants and corporate finance teams preparing merger proxy statements, Form S-4/F-4, Form 8-K and Rule 3-05 disclosures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how Rule 3-05 financial statements and related audit/age/GAAP/reconciliation requirements apply in mergers, acquisitions and registration/proxy filings — including special rules for FPIs, foreign acquirees and EGC timing exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant financial statements required in target's merger proxy when financing not assured
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant’s financial statements for the two most recent fiscal years required to be filed and the current interim period since the last audited balance sheet must be included in Target’s merger proxy when the registrant has not demonstrated that financing is assured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies when registrant (acquirer) has entered agreement to purchase target but (a) does not have an unconditional firm commitment for financing and (b) registrant has not filed required Rule 3-05 financial statements for a recently acquired entity. Inclusion is required because registrant has not demonstrated financial ability to satisfy merger terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of acquirer's recently-acquired entity (Rule 3-05) financial statements in target proxy
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant has not previously filed the required Rule 3-05 financial statements of a recently acquired entity, those financial statements may need to be included in Target’s merger proxy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: that information generally would be considered material to Target shareholders’ voting decision. However, because only Target shareholders are voting, the SEC staff may grant relief from this requirement in appropriate circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: EGC timing exception for target’s required financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: SEC staff will not object to inclusion of two years of annual financial statements (and interim financial statements) in a merger proxy if both: (1) the merger proxy is filed after the legal acquirer’s IPO but before the filing (or filing deadline) of the legal acquirer’s first Form 10-K; and (2) the legal acquirer is an EGC that is not a shell company, or is a shell-company EGC (e.g., a SPAC EGC) and the target would be an EGC if it were conducting an IPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [FRM 10220.7] — timing and EGC status are the controlling considerations for this staff non-objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit requirements for financial statements in a merger proxy
rubrics_metrics.description: All annual financial statements included in a merger proxy statement (for both acquiring entity and target) must be audited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: for a target not subject to reporting under sections 13(a) or 15(d) of the 1934 Act, only the financial statements for the latest fiscal year must be audited if practicable; prior years need not be audited unless they were previously audited. [FRM 1140.5]

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance thresholds that trigger Rule 3-05 reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The significance thresholds that trigger Rule 3-05 financial statement filing requirements for acquisitions (including when either or both parties are foreign) are the same as when both acquirer and acquiree are domestic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These thresholds determine when filings such as Form 8-K, registration statements or proxy statements must include acquiree financials (e.g., >20% or >50% in various contexts). The staff diagram (section 2.1 reference) summarizes when Form 8-K filing or registration/proxy disclosure is required (e.g., acquired business >20% significance ordinarily triggers Form 8-K; various >50% rules apply to probable acquisitions and aggregated acquisitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of significance tests when acquiree and registrant use different GAAP
rubrics_metrics.description: To perform the significance tests for a foreign acquiree, the acquiree’s financial statement amounts used in the numerator must conform to the basis of accounting used by the registrant (i.e., amounts converted to registrant’s GAAP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A domestic registrant bases amounts on US GAAP. An FPI bases amounts on the basis it uses in its financial statements (US GAAP, IFRS IASB, or home-country GAAP with reconciliation). Therefore conversions may be necessary to perform significance calculations. [FRM 6350.2]

rubrics_metrics.name: When FPIs must provide Rule 3-05 financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: An FPI that files Form 20-F is not required to file a Form 8-K for business acquisitions; such an FPI is required to provide Rule 3-05 financial statements only when it files a registration statement (including a Form 20-F used to register shares under the 1934 Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing a registration statement, the FPI determines Rule 3-05 requirements based on Item 8 of Form 20-F (age of financial statements) and Item 17 of Form 20-F (content of financial statements). If the FPI instead elects US domestic reporting, the Form 8-K regime and Reg S-X requirements apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: FPI electing US domestic reporting: US GAAP requirement for US acquirees
rubrics_metrics.description: If an FPI files under US domestic reporting requirements and acquires a US acquiree, the Rule 3-05 financial statements for the US acquiree must be based on US GAAP and comply with Regulation S-X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In that situation, the rest of the chapter concerning foreign-acquiree accommodations is not relevant; US GAAP/Reg S-X rules govern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous offerings and shelf registration requirements for FPIs
rubrics_metrics.description: For continuous offerings, an FPI must file updated financial statements as required by S-X Rule 3-05 on a post-effective amendment during the offering period. For delayed offerings on a shelf registration, previously filed Rule 3-05 financial statements must comply with the age requirements at the time of each offering/takedown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [FRM 6230] — age and update obligations apply throughout the offering/shelf term; timeliness must be assessed at each takedown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable bases for preparation of Rule 3-05 financial statements for foreign acquirees
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements of foreign acquirees do not need to be prepared under US GAAP; acceptable bases include US GAAP, IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the IASB, or home-country GAAP reconciled to either US GAAP or IFRS IASB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 6.3.40 discusses acceptable bases, reconciliation requirements, and when reconciliations are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of periods required for Rule 3-05 financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of periods of Rule 3-05 financial statements required for a foreign acquiree are the same as the number required for all significant acquisitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See section 4.2.10 for the standard period requirements (annual periods and interim periods as applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Age requirements for Rule 3-05 financial statements (domestic vs foreign business)
rubrics_metrics.description: Age requirements for significant acquisitions are governed by S-X Rule 3-01 and Rule 3-02 for most acquisitions; however, if the acquiree is a foreign entity that meets the definition of a 'foreign business', the age requirements are those in Item 8 of Form 20-F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant must determine which age regime applies (Reg S-X vs Form 20-F Item 8) based on whether the acquiree meets the foreign business definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'foreign business' under S-X Rule 1-02(l)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'foreign business' is a business that: (1) is majority owned by persons who are not citizens or residents of the United States; (2) is not organized under the laws of the United States or any state thereof; and (3) either (a) more than 50% of its assets are located outside the United States, or (b) the majority of its executive officers and directors are not United States citizens or residents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In determining majority ownership, the SEC staff considers the ultimate parent entity that would consolidate the business under US GAAP (or IFRS IASB for IFRS issuers) and the parent’s controlling shareholders. Examples illustrate application to holdings, carve-outs and mixed-jurisdiction entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation requirements when acquiree financials are not based on US GAAP
rubrics_metrics.description: When Rule 3-05 financial statements are required for a foreign acquiree that does not prepare financial statements using US GAAP, they must be reconciled to US GAAP in certain instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a reconciliation is required depends in part on whether the acquiree meets the definition of a foreign business and on the basis of accounting used; section 6.3.40 explains the reconciliation triggers and mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability of FPIs to use pro forma information to determine significance
rubrics_metrics.description: A foreign registrant that voluntarily files audited financial statements of a significant acquired business on a Form 6-K may use pro forma financial information reflecting previous significant acquisitions as the basis for determining significance of subsequent acquisitions if specific conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: the registrant has filed Rule 3-05 (or Rule 3-14 for real estate) financial statements for each such previous significant acquired business, and the registrant has filed the pro forma financial information required by Article 11 for previously acquired/disposed businesses. Prior registration statements that incorporated required information may also satisfy conditions (see Question 3.3.110).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing/filing windows affecting required periods and age (Form 8-K timing examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing deadlines and the timing of registration/proxy effectiveness determine which periods and ages of acquiree financial statements must be included (e.g., Form 8-K due within three months after acquired business’s year-end; due more than three months after year-end; registration effective more than six or nine months after year-end).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Various examples and Q&A (sections 6.3.60–6.3.110 and examples 6.3.50–6.3.110) illustrate the consequences of different filing dates and registration effectiveness dates for which periods and ages must be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditing standards for audits of foreign acquiree Rule 3-05 financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The financial statements included under Rule 3-05 must be audited; specific auditing standards applicable to audits of foreign acquiree Rule 3-05 financial statements are addressed in the guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See section 6.3.250 for discussion of which auditing standards (and when) are used in the audit of a foreign acquiree’s Rule 3-05 financial statements; auditors and registrants should consult that section for specifics.
